data.narrative:
Xtend, a Series B defense and security company founded by Aviv Shapira, has raised $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 8 private-stage peers and 2 public companies in the Defense & Security sector.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression uses the $100M raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying a $190M valuation. The peer-median method references 8 same-sector, same-stage companies with valuations ranging from $300M to $3.0B. Named peers include Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B), yielding a median peer valuation of $1.1B.

The two methods produce a wide dispersion. The stage-progression method, relying solely on capital raised, yields $190M. The peer-median method, anchored to actual market comparables, yields $1.1B. Triangulation across both methods supports a range of $162M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $658M. The substantial gap between methods reflects uncertainty around Xtend's relative competitive standing within the peer set and the degree to which it has achieved the traction or market position of higher-valued comparables. Resolution of this uncertainty requires clarity on revenue, growth rate, and operational metrics relative to named peers.
